_origin: Adapted from a public postmortem; names, times and numbers changed.

incident.title: ServiceRegistryWritesSlow
incident.description: service-registry (5-node cluster used for service discovery and config by every backend service): p50 key-value write latency 2.1s (normal under 300ms). Backend services timing out on registry lookups; game sessions failing to start (58% failure).

initial_context: Shown before any check. Registry node reg-03 fired disk-latency alerts last Thursday and again at 19:48 today (fsync p99 180ms for two minutes); a hardware ticket for it is open with the vendor. Changes in the last 48 hours: registry 'streaming' delivery mode being rolled out to more client services (started yesterday; planned CPU saving); 18:10 today matchmaking-api v12.8; Tuesday registry-client library bump in 40 services. Traffic is at its weekly Saturday peak.

hypotheses.hardware: A failing disk or node in the registry cluster is slowing writes.
hypotheses.streaming: A recent registry configuration change is degrading its performance.
hypotheses.matchmaking_release: The matchmaking-api v12.8 deploy is overloading the registry.
hypotheses.load: Peak traffic is more than the registry cluster can handle.
hypotheses.storage: The registry's on-disk data store has grown or fragmented, making writes slow.

node_health.description: Per-node disk, CPU and memory health for the 5 registry nodes, and write latency per node.
node_health.result: All 5 nodes pass disk health checks. reg-03: fsync p99 180ms from 19:48 to 19:50, 4ms since; the other nodes 3-5ms throughout. Write latency is the same on every node, leader (reg-01) and followers alike: p50 2.0-2.2s, including during reg-03's normal periods. CPU 55-62% on each node.

request_rate.description: Requests to the registry per second, by client service.
request_rate.result: Total 410k/s at 19:50, vs 395k/s at the same time last Saturday. matchmaking-api: 22k/s before and after its 18:10 deploy. No client grew by more than 6% day over day.

latency_history.description: Registry write latency p50 over the last 36 hours, alongside recent change events.
latency_history.result: p50 write latency 180-260ms until 19:35 today, including last Saturday's peak at the same load. Streaming reached 50% of traffic-routing clients at 15:00 today: p50 290ms. 100% at 19:30: p50 900ms at 19:40, 2.1s at 19:50.

registry_profile.description: Goroutine and lock profile of the registry leader, 19:55 UTC.
registry_profile.result: 71% of write-path time blocked waiting on a single channel in the streaming event publisher (stream.Publish -> eventBuffer.append). 4,300 goroutines queued on it. Before streaming (profile from last week): no single wait point above 4%.

store_stats.description: Size and write timings of the registry's embedded data store on the leader.
store_stats.result: Data file 1.3GB, 11% free pages, same as a month ago. Store commit time p99 6ms. Compaction last ran 02:00 UTC, normal.

matchmaking_changes.description: matchmaking-api v12.8 change summary and its registry calls.
matchmaking_changes.result: 'Tune queue timeouts for weekend events.' Registry reads per request unchanged (1); registry writes: none. Canary at 17:40 showed no registry latency change.

registry_logs.result: QUERY FAILED: log search timed out after 30s (the log pipeline discovers its shards through the registry). 0 lines returned. This is a failed query, not an empty result.

cdn_bandwidth.description: CDN bandwidth for game asset downloads.
cdn_bandwidth.result: 1.9 Tbps, 4% above last Saturday; a new game release at 18:00 drove extra downloads. No errors.

payment_provider.result: Provider reports degraded card authorisations in Brazil since 19:10 UTC. 0.4% of purchases affected.

build_queue.result: 31 builds queued, median wait 6 minutes. Two runners offline for maintenance.

guidance: A failed query (like a timeout or a locked table) means the check itself could not complete. It is not evidence that nothing happened. An empty result from a wrong service name means the query was malformed, not that there is nothing to find. Neither should be cited as evidence in a root cause analysis.
